table_title: For every tennis player who has won at least one Grand Slam singles title in the Open Era (1968 onwards), give their Open Era singles-title count, their tour (men's or women's), their nationality at the time of their title-winning career, and whether they have won more than five Grand Slam singles titles in the Open Era.
db_analog: SELECT p.player_name AS player, COUNT(t.title_id) AS grand_slam_singles_titles, p.tour, p.title_winning_nationality AS nationality, (COUNT(t.title_id) > 5) AS qualifies FROM tennis_players p JOIN grand_slam_singles_titles t ON t.player_id = p.id WHERE t.is_open_era = TRUE GROUP BY p.id HAVING COUNT(t.title_id) >= 1 ORDER BY COUNT(t.title_id) DESC, p.player_name ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of Grand Slam men's singles champions', 'List of Grand Slam women's singles champions', 'Open Era tennis records – Men's singles', and 'Open Era tennis records – Women's singles', all accessed 2026-05-12. The universe is 119 unique tennis players (58 men + 61 women) who have won at least one Grand Slam singles title in the Open Era (1968 onwards). The Open Era cutoff is the canonical pre-Open-vs-Open transition (the 1968 French Open being the first Open Era major); titles won before 1968 in the amateur era are excluded from the per-player counts even for careers spanning the transition (Margaret Court 11 Open Era of 24 lifetime; Billie Jean King 8 of 12; Rod Laver 5 of 11; Ken Rosewall 4 of 8; John Newcombe 5 of 7). The comparator Qualifies (>5) is strictly 'more than 5' (i.e., ≥ 6 Open Era titles): 24 of 119 players qualify (13 men + 11 women). Title counts are current through the 2026 Australian Open for both tours — the most recent completed Grand Slam tournament as of the source-access date. Active players whose counts may still increment include Djokovic, Alcaraz, Sinner, Świątek, Sabalenka, and Gauff (temporal_sensitivity = medium reflects this). Nationality is the nationality the player represented in their title-winning matches (majority-of-wins rule for split-career players): Lendl Czechoslovak (all 8 titles won pre-1992 naturalization); Seles Yugoslav (8 of 9 titles won 1990-1993 pre-naturalization); Navratilova American (all 18 titles won 1978+ as US-resident/citizen); Kriek South African (1-1 flag split between 1981 AO South African and 1982 AO US; chronologically-first tiebreaker under the flag-grounded rule); Rybakina Kazakhstani (both Open Era titles 2022 Wimbledon and 2026 Australian Open as Kazakhstani after 2018 federation switch); Graf and Becker German (West-German-flag titles 1985-1989 and German-flag titles 1990+ are normalized to a single 'German' value after the 1990 reunification — the master listings switch the flag mid-career).
_extraction_notes: Comparative instance: tests whether the model can compute per-player Grand Slam title counts (Open Era only) and apply the >5 comparator correctly across both qualifiers (~20%) and non-qualifiers (~80% of universe). Universe = 119 unique Open Era Grand Slam singles champions per the 2 master Wikipedia tournament articles, cross-validated against the 2 Open Era records pages. Schema: 5 cols (Player PK + Titles + Tour + Nationality + Qualifies (>5) boolean). Tour distribution: 58 Men's, 61 Women's. Title distribution (most prolific): Djokovic 24, Serena 23, Nadal 22, Graf 22, Federer 20, Evert 18, Navratilova 18, Sampras 14, Borg 11, Court 11. 24 qualifiers (>5): 13 men + 11 women — Men: Djokovic, Nadal, Federer, Sampras, Borg, Connors, Lendl, Agassi, McEnroe, Wilander, Alcaraz, Edberg, Becker. Women: Serena, Graf, Evert, Navratilova, Court, Seles, King, Goolagong Cawley, Henin, Venus, Świątek. Sort order: Grand Slam Singles Titles DESC, Player ASC. Nationality rule: nationality at title-winning per the country flag shown in the master tournament-listing articles (cross-validated by the per-player country flag in the Open Era records pages), with majority-of-wins for split-career players and chronologically-first as tiebreaker for 1-1 flag splits — Lendl Czechoslovak (all 8 with Czechoslovak flag), Seles Yugoslav (8 of 9 with Yugoslav flag), Navratilova American (all 18 with US flag), Kriek South African (1-1 split, chronologically-first tiebreaker = 1981 South African flag), Rybakina Kazakhstani (both Open Era titles with Kazakhstan flag), Graf and Becker German. For Margaret Court and Billie Jean King, Open Era titles only are counted (excludes amateur era 1968- titles). For Rod Laver, Ken Rosewall, John Newcombe (careers spanning 1968), same rule. Boolean Qualifies (>5) uses strict 'more than 5' semantics (>5, equivalent to ≥6); Sharapova and Hingis at exactly 5 are FALSE. Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles + painters-cycle + extinctions-cycles + deserts-cycles lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Player (Wikipedia article-title name); (b) per-row data sourced from 2 master Grand Slam articles + 2 Open Era records articles for cross-validation; (c) explicit relation commitment for the Open Era cutoff (1968 onwards strict); (d) deterministic Nationality rule for split-career players (majority-of-wins); (e) explicit Tour rule (Men's / Women's, two values only — no mixed-doubles or other formats counted); (f) explicit comparator semantics (>5 = ≥6 strict); (g) source-defined universe (all Open Era Grand Slam singles champions per master Wikipedia articles, no curator selection within universe).
